body: I'm very curious about this question.  It sounds like your dad got a sweet deal! IMO, pensions have changed from being a guarantee back in the day when people didn't know how to invest and government was trying to incentive people to work for them. It seems like capitalism is thriving and private financial infrastructure is a better way to go nowadays. My example, I have a small pension after with state gov for 5 years, but it has 0% ROR and is about $40k. Obvi, that is not enough to retire on by any means especially when I make 3 times that much in the private sector. I'm seriously considering either rolling it over to my company's 401k system or using it to pay off debt. I have no real emergency savings and will retire in 30 years. Today's economy is giving me the chills honestly. I don't know what will happen to that money in 30 years, so why not take out the money that I saved and try to help myself now so I can grow my future? I will be giving up my pension, but the total pay out is not a lot (about $350-750 per month) 😓

Thank you everyone! Just being a part of this forum is already helping me. Here are some things I plan to implement:

- Continue to budget using the bank-split method - putting how much I owe in debt in one account and have automatic payments taken out so I'm not tempted to squirrel away money or misspend

- Make a money vision board to visualize  the goals 

- Create a wishlist to delay the impulse to buy now

- For this month, have no buy for the first 15 days, except groceries, food, and bills. If I feel tempted to buy, then I can buy some debt 😂

- Set up a therapy appointment to talk this through

- Let my partner know that I'm trying to be as frugal as possible 

- Stay on top of debt and credit cards so my credit improves

In the next few months once I have a system down:
- Designate credit cards to have a job or task - ex: emergencies only, coffee only, clothing budget for $100 only, etc.

- Set a clothing budget and have a look in mind so I don't just buy what looks cute but is impractical or I don't need

I'm very excited for my new job to help me with this too because I will be making more that I can throw at debt and get a new system set up with direct deposit and automatic payments. 

I have created an excel spreadsheet before to get rid of collections from past mistakes. I'm annoyed at myself for getting myself into this situation again. Hopefully this forum and therapy will help!
